parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence and no sodomy law, but the operative exposure is state actors: a May 2026 warrantless raid detaining ~30 people with extortion and fabricated charges, plus documented post-2024-election persecution of LGBTQ people. These are recent, state-involved incidents, not dated history. Recourse is thin: no gender-identity anti-discrimination law, no hate-crime statute, no legal gender recognition, and a visitor cannot obtain matching documents. Positives are real but mostly climate signals: Pride participation, a trans legislator, and 2023 polls showing majority support for equal rights. Combined regime: police hostility with weak remedies sits in Elevated Risk, not the tier of routine trans-specific custody or facility mandates.

entry_documents.exposure: No working legal gender recognition; 2027-style court route never granted. A trans visitor's foreign passport stands, but mismatched presentation risks scrutiny with no recognition framework to appeal to.
entry_documents.protection: Dossier does not document border officers rejecting foreign documents; visitor uses home passport.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch during any police stop can escalate into fabrication of charges, as the 2026 raid shows.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: May 2026 warrantless raid on an LGBTQ+ venue detained ~30 people; officers extorted detainees and charged a nonexistent offence. State actors as perpetrators, recent and patterned with 2024 political-crisis persecution.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Same-sex conduct is not criminalised, so the 'homosexuality' charge had no legal basis; NGOs denounced the raid publicly.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention with fabricated charges shows recourse is thin where police manufacture the offence.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Raid occurred in one state/province; no other regional variation documented. No facility or custody placement rules for trans visitors documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Uncertainty outside that state is unevidenced expectation, not safety.

care_services.exposure: Law sets no general healthcare or transition-care provisions; no guarantee a visitor's trans status or medication needs are protected if discovered during care.
care_services.protection: Not documented for visitors; emergency care rules unaddressed.
care_services.interaction: Medical discovery could feed into the same police scrutiny documented in the raid.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police framed detainees as 'committing the crime of homosexuality' — threat-framing by the state itself; 2024 reporting describes intensified persecution of LGBTQ people after the disputed election.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No criminalisation of same-sex conduct or trans identity; government participates in Pride; a trans candidate won legislative office.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Acceptance signals are national climate; the operative encounters documented are hostile police action.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. A parent travelling with a minor shares the raid-and-extortion exposure if identified as LGBTQ, and no anti-discrimination protection covers them.
minors_guardians.protection: Supreme court 2016 ruling protects families without distinction in civil registry — resident-facing, climate signal only.
minors_guardians.interaction: Child's presence could intensify scrutiny during any police stop; no custody or family-law protection for visitors documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police extortion and warrantless detention documented; a 2015 prisoner-of-conviction case shows state custody of an openly gay politician. No dedicated penalty for bias violence and no hate-crime statute.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2023 poll: majority supports equal rights for LGBTIQ people; international monitors publicly denounce abuses.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Civil-society denunciation has not stopped the raids, so oversight functions as exposure confirmation.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law, no hate-crime aggravation, no LGR route; 2016 ID-card announcement has no implementing procedure. Post-election persecution reported 2024 with no recorded remedy.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have issued pro-LGBT-family rulings; NGOs and an asylum agency profile provide monitoring; same-sex conduct legal.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper legality did not prevent raid or extortion; functioning institutions are not shown working for trans people here.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: police stop, confiscation/extortion, release without lawful basis, courts unlikely to deliver remedy. Lower severity here because no trans-specific criminal statute exists and the bogus charge was publicly denounced; higher because the raid is recent, patterned with 2024 political persecution.

Similar tier: routine exposure to official scrutiny, documented detention and humiliation, prosecutions uncommon, inconsistent enforcement, scarce legal aid. This dossier adds a concrete state-actor extortion incident but lacks a standing 'deception' statute on the books.

Lower than 0.65-A: there national equality law protects gender identity and a complaint produced apology and compensation. Here there is no gender-identity anti-discrimination law and no documented working remedy after state-run detention, so recourse cannot lift the score into Reduced Risk.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime pairs weak formal criminalisation with real state-actor hostility. Same-sex conduct is legal and polls show majority support, but there is no gender-identity protection, no hate-crime penalty, and no legal recognition a visitor could invoke. The heaviest evidence is the May 2026 warrantless raid with extortion and fabricated charges, corroborated by 2024 post-election persecution — both recent, state-involved, and met with denunciation but no remedy. That places worst documented conduct at state-tolerated targeting (tier 2) rather than routine imprisonment or universal facility mandates, holding the rating in Elevated Risk. Traveller with a minor inherits the same exposure; no minor-specific mitigation is documented.
